candidates.title: The Narrow Win
candidates.pitch: A concept mod for a poker-and-jokers roguelike in which a new stake changes what winning means: you must land inside a score band, because overshooting the blind busts the hand. The visitor is dealt eight cards and a five-slot joker rack full of runaway multipliers plus new throttle jokers, and has to find the one play and joker order that lands in the window. A solver then reveals how many of the thousands of plays were valid, so each puzzle has a rarity score you can brag about.
candidates.whyNow: Timeless: the community keeps building toward ever bigger numbers, and a stake that punishes excess flips every instinct a returning player has. Nothing similar has shipped here yet, so it is fresh.

research.summary: Base-game scoring is a chips times mult product where jokers resolve left to right, so order matters (multiplying effects want to sit after additive ones). Stakes stack extra penalties, and special starting decks already twist the scoring formula (one equalizes chips and mult), which shows rule-twisting concepts fit the genre. A large unbalanced mod exists purely to push numbers higher, so the community appetite for runaway scaling is real; a stake that punishes overshoot is the mirror image. The 'closest without going over' rule from a famous bidding game is the familiar precedent that makes the band easy to explain. All numbers on the page would be invented concept values, labelled as such.

facts.claim: As of 2026-10-10, community guides agree that jokers in the base game resolve left to right, so placing additive-mult jokers before multiplying ones raises the total.
A community calculator models a hand score as chips times mult, with multiplying effects applied after additive mult.
Base-game stakes stack: each harder stake keeps the earlier penalties and adds another, and the Green stake raises blind requirements faster each ante.
A base-game starting deck equalizes chips and mult when scoring and doubles the blind requirement, so decks that twist the scoring formula already exist.
The Cryptid mod describes itself as ignoring balance and relies on a helper mod for very large numbers; commenters in a Sep 2024 thread describe it as intentionally broken.
In the famous pricing show's opening bid round, the closest bid that does not go over the price wins.
Reported unconfirmed: one thesis example shows blind targets of 300, 450 and 600 in Ante 1 (big blind 1.5x small, boss 2x small).

inspirations: golf scoring (lower is better, exact is best)

design.coreLoop: Read the day's deal and band, drag cards into a play and jokers into rack order, watch the engine tally chips times mult step by step, then lock in. Land inside the band to clear, bust if you overshoot, fizzle if you undershoot. The solver then shows how many valid plays existed, awarding a rarity grade; tighter stakes (band widths shrinking from loose to razor thin) and the swinging-window rule keep the tenth puzzle as tense as the first.
sophisticationHooks: A real scoring engine (hand types with levels, card chips, additive and multiplying jokers resolving left to right) plus new throttle jokers such as a clamp, a bleed-off and a handshake pair that only works when two throttles sit apart
An exhaustive solver over all 218 plays of eight cards times up to 120 joker orders (about 26,000 evaluations), giving exact counts of valid solutions, a par, and a rarity score
A stake explorer that runs thousands of seeded deals in a worker and plots how often a random deal has any solution as the band narrows, so the visitor sees where the stake becomes cruel

A swinging-window mode where the target band alternates between a low and a high window across three hands, so the player must plan the whole sequence; seed, rack and play live in the URL hash for sharing
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: scoring engine and joker data module, seeded dealer, solver and stake-explorer worker, puzzle UI with keyboard and touch card and rack handling, step-by-step score tape, band meter with bust and fizzle animations, daily seed plus free sandbox, hash state, about and making-of panel with verified sources. Cut: custom art for real-game assets (all cards and jokers are drawn with CSS and SVG), full-run progression, sound beyond optional tiny synth ticks, user-written joker scripting.
risks: The base-game formula details come from community guides, so the page labels its rules as a fan concept with invented numbers and shows no game art or names beyond a plain reference.
The blind ratio claim rests on one thesis and stays unverified: the page does not state it as fact, it uses its own invented targets.
Joker interactions could multiply into untestable edge cases; mitigation: keep the engine to six effect types and test it against a hand-computed table before the UI is wired.
A puzzle with no valid solution frustrates; the dealer must reject unsolvable seeds using the solver before publishing the daily.

candidates.title: Fine Print Jokers
candidates.pitch: A joker family for a poker roguelike where every joker is a contract: a big boon now, and a clause that bills you later in score. The visitor assembles a five-joker rack of IOU jokers, balloon-payment jokers and co-signing pairs that split each other's debts, then plays a four-hand round against a blind and watches a ledger waterfall show each bill landing. A worker simulates thousands of seeded rounds to reveal exactly when borrowing against your future score beats playing it clean, and when it ends in a stamped default notice.
candidates.whyNow: Timeless: a debt economy is a rule family the community has not claimed, and the break-even curve is the sort of result people screenshot and argue about. Nothing like it has shipped here yet.

research.summary: Base-game scoring is chips times mult with jokers resolving left to right, and the genre already uses debt-adjacent ideas: one joker lets the player spend below zero, and a harder stake adds rented jokers that charge every round (the latter reported in beta coverage and left unconfirmed here). Starting decks already bend rules (one trades a hand for a joker slot, one pays for unused hands), which shows deck and joker families with trade-offs are a natural mod unit. A big unbalanced mod proves the audience wants strange rule families. No existing joker family is built around deferred score debt with transferable bills, so the angle is open. The page uses only invented chip debts and says it is a simulation, not financial advice.

facts.claim: As of 2026-10-10, a guide and community posts agree that a base-game joker (Credit Card) lets the player go into debt, up to 20 dollars per the guide.
Base-game starting decks already trade one resource for another, for example one deck gives an extra joker slot at the cost of one hand each round.
Community guides agree that jokers resolve left to right, so order changes the final score.
The Cryptid mod describes itself as ignoring balance, and commenters in a Sep 2024 thread describe it as intentionally broken.
Reported unconfirmed: a 2024 beta patch described a stake whose rental jokers charge a fee every round, per one outlet.
Reported unconfirmed: the base game pays interest on held cash up to a per-round cap, per one guide.

inspirations: Balatro jokers and the Credit Card idea
payday-loan and balloon-mortgage shapes (as satire of legalese)

design.coreLoop: Pick contract jokers for the rack, set the round target, and play a seeded four-hand round: each hand scores with the boon, then the ledger collects any bills that fall due. Read the waterfall, tweak order or swap a clause, and press the simulate button to see the win rate across thousands of seeded rounds versus a clean build. The break-even slider on target difficulty keeps rewarding experiments because leverage only wins in a specific band.
sophisticationHooks: A scoring and ledger engine: chips times mult resolved left to right, with five contract types (net-due IOU, escalating bill, balloon payment, revolving minimum, handshake co-sign that splits two neighbours' bills) and a default rule that rolls unpaid bills forward with a penalty
A worker Monte Carlo that plays a greedy bot through thousands of seeded rounds and draws win-rate, score histogram and the leverage break-even curve against target difficulty
A waterfall chart of the round (boons rising, bills falling due) drawn in SVG, with a stamped default notice and receipt-style share card as the moment of delight
Seeded audit challenges (for example beat target N using at most two contracts) and a URL-hash build code so friends can compare racks
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: engine and contract data, seeded deck and hand dealer, bot, worker simulation, rack builder with keyboard and drag, waterfall and histogram charts, break-even sweep, daily audit seed, hash state, about panel. Cut: full run structure with shops, more than five contract types, animated repo scenes beyond a single stamp, any art from the real game.
risks: Debt vocabulary must read as playful and simulated: chips only, a visible 'simulated, not financial advice' line, no real-money framing or gambling prompts.
The rental and interest facts are single-source and stay unverified, so the page cites them as 'as of 2026-10-10, per <source>' or omits them; the engine uses invented rates.
Contract interactions could make balance opaque; mitigation: cap the clause types at five and test the engine against a hand-computed ledger table.
Greedy bot may under-represent skilled play; the page labels the win rate as 'for a simple bot' and also offers a hand-play mode.
